classes.doc: SPIKE_1.2_PLANET_DETERMINISM.md. FRAME: Location is ABSOLUTE - zero world origin - not the sender's local frame. The server and every client rebase their origins independently (UCosmicDemoManager::UpdateWorldOrigin), so a local-frame position means nothing to the receiver. This is the same trick FRepMovement plays with RebaseOntoZeroOrigin/RebaseOntoLocalOrigin; we do it by hand off UWorld::OriginLocation so no engine-private header is involved. PRECISION: doubles, deliberately. These bodies sit at ~1e7 cm and players WALK on them; a float has ~1 cm of resolution out there and the surface col…

properties.name: ServerTime
properties.doc: arrival time is jittery - the observed spread was 0.03-0.57 s. Dead reckoning turns that jitter straight into position error at (velocity x jitter), which is invisible on a parked planet (20 cm/s gave 10 cm) and brutal on a moving one: at the 9200 cm/s these bodies actually orbit at, the same jitter produced a 100-550 cm wobble, spiking to 4792 cm during a load hitch. Predicted 4968. It was not a tuning problem. With a server stamp, the client can place every snapshot on the SERVER's timeline and play them back against a clock of its own, so arrival jitter becomes a small constant delay instead of positional noise. double, not float: a shard up for a day is at 86400 s, where float resolution is ~8 ms - the same order as the thing being measured.

Two decoupled gravity knobs (deliberate game-design fakery): OrbitalGM - mu = G*M used to attract OTHER celestial bodies (orbits). SurfaceGravity - walking gravity at the surface; falls off as (R/r)^2.

functions.name: GetFrameRotationDelta
functions.doc: literally cannot tell 230 degrees one way from 130 the other. That is not a theoretical concern here. `APoolPlanet::MaxPoolSpin` is 12 rad/s and the 09-02 bomb runs hitched to **335 ms a frame**, which is 4.02 rad = 230 degrees of genuine rotation in a single tick. The pose difference is unusable there, and the sanity guard that used to sit on it (a quarter turn, meant to reject teleports) fired on every one of those frames and dropped the ride entirely - which is exactly "the camera still can't keep it clamped down after a bunch of bombs go off". Bombs raise the spin toward the cap, the cap plus a hitch exceeds the guard, and the guard throws away the correct answer. Angular velocity has no wrap and no ambiguity, and it is authoritative on both sides of the wire (box3d on the server, the replicated pose on a client), so this is frame-rate independent by construction.

functions.doc: This body's angular velocity in rad/s, world space, valid on BOTH sides: the live box3d body where there is one, the last replicated snapshot on a client. Unlike the frame delta this does not require the body to have ticked yet, so a caller in an earlier tick group can still use it.

functions.name: SetSurfaceCollisionActive
functions.doc: Proximity-gated collision swap. Active = walk on the real per-triangle mesh surface (exact landings, walkable heightmap terrain) with the cheap analytic sphere off; inactive = analytic sphere on (catches landings from flight), mesh collision off. Driven by UpdateSurfaceCollision so only the planet a player stands on pays the cost. VIRTUAL because the base implementation assumes `Mesh` is where this body's geometry lives. That is true for spheres, dice and the star, but NOT for tetromino pool planets, which hide `Mesh` entirely and build themselves out of BlockISM instances - see APoolPlanet's override.

functions.name: HasCelestialAuthority
functions.doc: Does THIS machine simulate this body? Net mode, not IsRunningDedicatedServer() and not bPinned. We have been bitten by the process-level check before (the shard heartbeat silently never fired under PIE because IsRunningDedicatedServer() is per-PROCESS and PIE runs client and server in one). NM_Client is the only mode that must not simulate: standalone, listen server and dedicated all own it.

functions.name: GetBodyAngularVelocity
functions.sig: virtual FVector GetBodyAngularVelocity() const { return FVector::ZeroVector; }
functions.doc: Angular velocity of whatever actually drives this body, rad/s. Zero for a plain orbiting body (the integrator is point masses and does not spin anything); APoolPlanet overrides it with the box3d body's spin.

functions.name: GetMaxAngularSpeed
functions.doc: solver is also asked to respect it (APoolPlanet::Tick) is then a performance measure, not the guarantee. WHY THIS IS NOT LEFT TO THE SOLVER CLAMP. On 2026-09-05, with a freshly deployed server and MaxPoolSpin at 1.75, a client measured its ride body at **407 rad/s** and 16.5 km/s - 230x and 55x their caps. The per-tick clamp in APoolPlanet::Tick is unreachable on a client by design (that Tick returns early without authority) and, on the server, runs AFTER ACelestialBody::Tick has already published the pose, so the wire carries the pre-clamp value by construction. A cap enforced in one place that several paths route around is not a cap. Defaults are deliberately loose - they exist to catch garbage, not to govern anything. A body with real limits overrides them (see APoolPlanet).

functions.name: PublishServerPose
functions.doc: Server: publish the current pose if it has moved enough to be worth a packet.

functions.name: TickReplicatedPose
functions.doc: Client: dead-reckon from the last snapshot and decay the visual error.

functions.name: SampleLocation
functions.doc: Pose at a given point on the SERVER's timeline, in this machine's local frame. Interpolates between the two buffered snapshots when the time falls between them, and extrapolates off the newer one when it does not.

properties.name: Radius
properties.doc: Body radius in cm (visual + gameplay).

properties.name: OrbitalGM
properties.doc: mu = G*M (cm^3/s^2) used to attract other celestial bodies. 0 = attracts nothing.

properties.name: SurfaceGravity
properties.doc: Walking/pull gravity at the surface (cm/s^2). 980 = Earth. For black holes this is the pull at the event horizon (make it huge).

properties.name: bPinned
properties.doc: Pinned bodies (the sun, the black hole) do not move.

properties.name: InitialVelocity
properties.doc: Initial orbital velocity (cm/s).

properties.name: EventHorizonRadius
properties.doc: Black hole only: bodies inside this radius are consumed. Grows as it eats.

properties.name: PullRadius
properties.doc: Black hole only: pull + infall drag applies inside this radius.

properties.name: ShellMaterial
properties.doc: Optional second sphere drawn slightly above the surface: lava on stars, ocean on water planets. Enabled when ShellMaterial is set.

properties.name: ShellMID
properties.doc: Per-body dynamic instance of ShellMaterial, so each planet can carry its own tint. Without one, SetMaterial hands every planet the same shared asset and AtmosphereColor reaches nothing you can see - which is exactly why all eight tints rendered as the material's authored blue.

properties.name: ShellScale
properties.doc: Shell radius as a multiple of Radius (1.02 = thin ocean layer).

properties.name: SurfaceSagFraction
properties.doc: How far the surface MESH sags inside its own nominal radius, as a fraction. A faceted sphere only touches Radius at its vertices; the middle of each facet sits R*(1-cos(pi/Segments)) inside it. SM_PlanetSphere has 192 segments, so 1 - cos(0.9375 deg) = 1.34e-4 - and the sun's ground probe measured 16 cm against a predicted 15. The analytic CollisionSphere is inset by this so the two colliders agree. Without it the floor steps by this amount whenever the body swaps between them, which the character feels as jitter and the build component turns into pieces floating above the ground you are standing on. Retessellate the sphere and this must follow it: 1 - cos(pi/Segments).

properties.name: bHasAtmosphere
properties.doc: --- Atmosphere rendering --- Enable atmospheric scattering rendering for this planet

properties.name: AtmosphereColor
properties.doc: Atmosphere tint (RGB). Drives BOTH the from-orbit shell glow and the from-ground SkyAtmosphere sky color, so the sky matches the planet's look from space. Default is Earth sky blue.

properties.name: AtmosphereTintStrength
properties.doc: colour, straight through. This was 0.0331 (RayleighReferenceScale) for one revision, on the assumption that M_Atmosphere's vector parameter is a physical Rayleigh coefficient. The asset says otherwise: it holds a Fresnel, a Multiply, a Constant, ONE texture parameter (AtmosphereLUT) and ONE vector parameter - the shape of a rim-glow shell where the vector is a straight TINT, not a coefficient. Scaling a tint by 0.0331 crushes it to near-black, which is why setting it produced no visible change at all. The physical coefficient on UAtmosphereComponent keeps RayleighReferenceScale, because there it really is one. Two different quantities, two different scales - conflating them is what cost the last two passes. Exposed so it can be dialled without a rebuild.

properties.name: AtmosphereName
properties.doc: Which named tint this body was given ("Red", "Blue", ...), or NAME_None. Gameplay asks for planets by this, never by comparing AtmosphereColor to a literal - a float compare against a colour breaks the first time a channel moves by 0.01, and it fails SILENTLY: whatever was filtering on it simply finds nothing, which looks identical to the feature not being written yet. Set from FCosmicAtmosphereTint by the world builder, from the same entry that set the colour, so the two cannot disagree.

properties.name: AtmosphereComponent
properties.doc: Optional atmosphere component (automatically created if bHasAtmosphere is true)

properties.name: SurfaceMesh
properties.doc: ConfigureVisuals applies it before anything reads Mesh->GetStaticMesh(), which matters because the shell and the collision swap both gate on that being non-null. THE SUN WAS INVISIBLE BECAUSE NOTHING EVER SET THIS. FCosmicFixedBody had no mesh field, the C++ builder had nothing to assign, and ACelestialBody only ever COPIED Mesh's mesh onto the shell - so a body spawned by the builder had a null mesh, a null shell, and rendered nothing at all while still lighting the scene and colliding. The old Python demo scripts set the mesh by hand, which is why this only appeared once the builder took over. Left null it falls back to the engine sphere rather than staying invisible. A grey ball is a bug you can see; nothing is a bug you go looking for.

properties.name: MeshStretch
properties.doc: Non-uniform stretch on the visual mesh (a lumpy potato, not an egg). Collision stays the analytic sphere.

properties.name: CollisionSphere
properties.doc: Exact analytic collision. The scaled render sphere's own collision sits ~0.5-2% above the visible surface, which reads as hovering on big bodies - this sphere is set slightly INSIDE the poly surface instead.

properties.name: ServerPose
properties.doc: The last snapshot the server sent. Clients read it; nothing else should.

classes.name: UCelestialSubsystem
classes.doc: Layer 1 of the custom physics stack: the celestial simulation. Double-precision N-body integration (semi-implicit Euler, fixed substeps) over registered ACelestialBody actors, black hole consumption/growth, and gravity queries for gameplay (walking gravity, black hole pull). This layer deliberately does NOT use a rigid-body engine - orbits are point masses. Local physics (dice, debris, characters) belongs to Box3D/Chaos.

functions.sig: void RequestImpulseAtPoint(ACelestialBody* Body, const FVector& WorldPoint, const FVector& DeltaV);
functions.doc: TryCreateBody is server-gated and a client has no box3d body at all. Neither logs anything, so from the client's seat the shot connects, the hit FX play, and the planet does not move. That was the whole of the "shooting planets does nothing" report. On the authority this dispatches immediately. On a client it is forwarded through the local player's UCosmicPlayerRepComponent - the Cosmos plugin's per-player replication channel; see that component's file header for why a generic carrier exists at all. functions.doc: The body the player is standing on. Its orbit FREEZES while anchored - a planet that teleports along its orbit under the character's feet causes violent ground shake. Null = nothing anchored. Defined in the .cpp, not inline: TWeakObjectPtr<ACelestialBody>'s assignment operator needs ACelestialBody to be a COMPLETE type at the point it is compiled, and this header only forward-declares it. That was silently fine as long as this header always happened to be pulled into a unity blob after something that had already included CelestialBody.h - until a TU compiles this header standalone (e.g. the adaptive build excluding a recently-touched .cpp from the unity file), at which point it fails with a wall of "no operator=" template noise pointing at WeakObjectPtrTemplates.h instead of at the real cause.

properties.doc: LEGACY. When true, the body a player stands on freezes its orbit. OFF by default and for this game: planets must never stop for a player (the player is carried along instead), and freezing is multiplayer-incompatible anyway.

The action bar is deliberately generic: slots are "Action 1..8", and the key that fires each one is rebindable in the options menu. The ability decides what it IS; the slot only decides where i…

properties.doc: The montage to play. Aurora's Primary_Attack_A/B/C_Montage already exist; plain AnimSequences need a montage wrapper before they can be used here.

properties.doc: Playback rate multiplier. Raise it to make a slow marketplace swing snappy without re-authoring the asset.

properties.doc: --- Damage ---

properties.name: Reach
properties.doc: How far the hit reaches, in cm.

properties.name: ArcHalfDeg
properties.doc: Half-angle of the damage cone, degrees. Ignored for AroundSelf.

properties.name: HitDelaySeconds
properties.doc: THE ZERO-LOCK WINDOW, in seconds from the key press to the damage landing. Nothing about the animation is ever locked - a new action always replaces the current one immediately. What this controls is whether the interrupted action got far enough to CONNECT. Press another key before this elapses and the pending hit is cancelled with it, so mashing produces a lot of motion and no damage, while a deliberate press lands. Set to 0 for an action that hits the instant it is pressed.

properties.name: HealSelf
properties.doc: One-shot heal applied to the CASTER the instant the action resolves.

properties.name: HealOverTime
properties.doc: Heal-over-time applied to the caster, HealOverTime per second for EffectDuration seconds. Backs Regeneration and similar.

properties.name: DamageOverTime
properties.doc: Damage-over-time applied to every target HIT, per second for EffectDuration seconds. Backs Poison, Burn, Bleed.

properties.name: EffectDuration
properties.doc: Duration in seconds for HealOverTime / DamageOverTime.

properties.name: LifestealFrac
properties.doc: Fraction of damage dealt returned to the caster as health (life-tap).

properties.name: ProjectileSpeed
properties.doc: Travel speed of the launched bolt, cm/s.

properties.name: ProjectileRadius
properties.doc: Collision radius of the bolt, cm.

properties.name: SplashRadius
properties.doc: Detonation / area-of-effect radius on impact. 0 = single-target direct hit.

properties.doc: Impulse handed to any box3d body the bolt strikes, so spells shove planets and debris like the ship weapons do.

properties.name: bProjectileGravity
properties.doc: Bend the bolt toward nearby gravity wells (arcing shots).

properties.name: Description
properties.doc: Spellbook blurb.

properties.name: UiColor
properties.doc: Icon / bolt tint used on the bar, the spellbook and the projectile.

Leave it unset and the component falls back to a built-in list of this project's two Paragon heroes - which is deprecated: it hard-codes /Game/... paths inside the plugin, so those references are invisible to the editor and a deleted asset breaks the swap with no warning anywhere. functions.name: UpdateSkyAtmosphere
functions.doc: Repositions a single SkyAtmosphere (and its sun light) onto whatever atmosphere-bearing planet the player is standing on, sized to that planet, with the sun aimed from the star; hides both in space. This is what gives a real Rayleigh blue sky from the surface, distinct from the per-planet shell glow seen from orbit.

functions.name: UpdateTimeDilation
functions.doc: Eases the celestial sim's TimeScale down as the player nears a body, so the world you're landing on/standing on is nearly still.

functions.name: UpdateWorldOrigin
functions.doc: Rebases the world origin to follow the player so collision/physics stay precise far from (0,0,0). This is the real fix for the landing bounce.

functions.name: UpdateSurfaceCollision
functions.doc: Proximity-gated walkable surface: switches each planet a player is near to real per-triangle mesh collision (and back to the cheap analytic sphere when everyone leaves). Gated by ANY player so it already works for multiple players on multiple planets.

functions.name: RescaleBodies
functions.doc: Cap landable-body radius to MaxPlanetRadius at startup (no script re-run needed). Idempotent.

properties.name: FlameSystem
properties.doc: Assigned to the player's CosmicFlightComponent.

properties.name: ExplosionSystem
properties.doc: Burst played where a destroyed ship comes apart. Optional.

properties.name: PlayerAbilitySet
properties.doc: The player character's action set (Action 1-6). Leave empty to use the built-in starter moveset, which works without any content authored.

properties.name: TrainingEnemyCount
properties.doc: Ground creatures dropped around the start pad at BeginPlay so there is something to fight immediately. 0 disables.

properties.name: TrainingEnemyRadius
properties.doc: How far from the pad they stand (cm).

properties.name: RespawnLocation
properties.doc: Respawn point after black hole death. Zero = player start location.

properties.name: SimTimeScale
properties.doc: Orbit simulation speed, pushed to UCelestialSubsystem::TimeScale at BeginPlay. The demo's orbital periods are physically scaled (the inner planet takes ~5 real hours per orbit, outer ones days), so at 1.0 nothing visibly moves - this is why "nothing orbits" while the sim is technically running. ~250 puts the inner system on a minute-scale orbit you can actually watch. Set to 1.0 for true-scale, 0.0 to pause.

properties.name: NearTimeScale
properties.doc: Sim speed used when the player is right at a planet's surface. The sim eases from this (near) up to SimTimeScale (deep space) over ~3 radii of altitude, so landing and walking happen on a near-still world while distant orbits still run fast. This is what stops planets streaking out from under your feet at full time scale.

properties.name: WorldRebaseThreshold
properties.doc: The world origin is rebased to follow the player once they drift beyond this many cm from it. Past a few thousand km, collision math loses float precision and the character capsule can't de-penetrate the planet ("stuck and failed to move" -> the landing bounce). 100 km keeps the active area sub-centimetre precise. 0 disables rebasing.

properties.name: WorldRebaseThresholdOnFoot
properties.doc: Tighter rebase distance used while the player is ON FOOT. Keeps the active coordinates small so surface collision/placement don't jitter from float precision. Loose (WorldRebaseThreshold) while flying so high-speed flight doesn't rebase every frame. Above the start platform's distance from the sun (~75 km) so the player spawning there does NOT trigger an immediate rebase (that startup rebase tripped the GPU-scene light ensure and halted PIE before the dice spawned). Landing on a distant planet (>1000 km out) still rebases once, which brings the player to the origin - so walking on a small planet stays precise.

properties.name: bPlanetCollisions
properties.doc: --- 3D-pool mode (pushed to the celestial subsystem at BeginPlay) --- Elastic planet-planet collisions (planets clack off each other).

properties.name: PoolBoundaryRadius
properties.doc: Bounce-wall radius from the origin (0 = no wall). Planets that reach it reflect back inward - the edges of the pool table.

properties.name: BounceRestitution
properties.doc: Restitution for planet/wall bounces (1 = perfectly elastic).

properties.name: bFreezeAnchoredBody
properties.doc: LEGACY freeze of the planet a player stands on. OFF - planets never stop for a player (the player rides the moving planet instead). Freezing is multiplayer-incompatible.

properties.name: PlayerTerminalVelocity
properties.doc: Falling terminal velocity for the player (cm/s). UE's default 4000 (=144 km/h) made the character fall much slower than the box3d dice; raise it.

properties.name: MaxPlanetRadius
properties.doc: Optional runtime cap on landable-body radius. DISABLED by default (0) - planet size is authored in setup_cosmic_demo.py so the editor and PIE agree. A runtime cap made them disagree (small in PIE, big in the editor), so it's off. Set > 0 only if you want a quick override without re-running the script.

properties.name: MountMesh
properties.doc: --- Mount / ship (shown in place of the character while flying with a Mount item equipped). Set these on this actor in the level - the flight component is created at runtime so it has no editor Details of its own. --- Ship mesh. Leave empty to keep the default cone placeholder. Point it at your own static mesh (e.g. /Game/Ships/SM_Scout) to replace it.

properties.name: MountMeshScale
properties.doc: Local scale for the ship mesh. The stock cone needs (1.6, 1, 3.2); a real ship asset usually wants (1, 1, 1) or smaller.

properties.name: MountMeshRotation
properties.doc: Local rotation for the ship mesh (align its nose to +X/forward).

properties.name: MountMeshOffset
properties.doc: Local offset for the ship mesh relative to the character root.

properties.name: MeleeSwingMovesets
properties.doc: DO have an `UpperBody` montage slot, and every montage in the project is authored for it, so a clip here is the fix. KEYED BY CHARACTER because montages are skeleton-bound: one clip cannot serve both heroes, and Montage_Play on the wrong skeleton returns 0 silently (§10). The key matches the appearance catalog's ids. Inside each moveset the clips are keyed by WEAPON TYPE, and one clip serves both hands - the off hand plays it mirrored. Seeded in the constructor with Aurora's and Zinx's surviving attack montages, so melee animates out of the box rather than waiting for someone to find this property. Clear an entry to disable that hero's swing animation; the swing itself still lands.

properties.name: HotbarAbilities
properties.doc: Editable ability hotbar. Leave empty to use the HUD's built-in defaults; add entries to author your own abilities as CockpitAbility data (name, icon, category, cooldown) with a keybind each.

properties.name: bEnableBox3DPusher
properties.doc: box3d dice-pusher capsule on the player (the dice-field stress test). OFF in the pool arena: pool planets run in a SCALED box3d space and the real-scale capsule would phantom-collide with them.

properties.name: bEnableSkyAtmosphere
properties.doc: --- Sky atmosphere (ground-level blue sky on landed planets) --- Master switch for the follow-the-planet SkyAtmosphere.

properties.name: SkyAltitudeFraction
properties.doc: The sky turns on when the player is within this fraction of the planet's radius above its surface (0.15 = the top 15% of a radius counts as "in the air"). Above that you're in space and the sky is hidden.

properties.name: SkySunIntensity
properties.doc: Directional sun brightness used only while a sky is active (lux). Tune to taste - higher = brighter daytime sky and stronger surface sun.

properties.name: bEnableFillLighting
properties.doc: --- Fill lighting + exposure (planet visibility) --- Master switch for the runtime fill lights + locked exposure. This is what stops metal/chrome planets reading as invisible dark mirrors against black space, and stops auto-exposure blowing nearby surfaces to pure white. NOTE: an earlier version of this used a real-time-capture SkyLight for the ambient instead of the second fill light below. Removed: with no permanent sky/cloud/IsSky-tagged mesh in view (our SkyAtmosphere is hidden except when standing on an atmosphere planet), the capture had nothing to see and came back pure black - the engine says as much ("A sky light with real-time capture ... Otherwise it will be black"), so it was doing nothing except paying for a scene capture every frame. Two static, non-shadow-casting fill directionals from different angles instead - cheaper, no capture, no warning.

properties.name: FillLightIntensity
properties.doc: Fill directional from roughly the opposite side of the key light, so no planet face is ever pure black (lux). Automotive metal materials are near- mirror (very low roughness), so a DIRECT light only paints a narrow specular hotspot rather than lighting the whole face the way a rough/diffuse surface would - pushed well above the old default to compensate, since there's no environment/ambient reflection source (see the note on the removed SkyLight above) to fill in the rest of a mirror surface.

properties.name: FillLight2Intensity
properties.doc: A second fill from a third angle (roughly above/behind), so a face that happens to point away from both the key and the first fill still isn't pure black. NOTE: a THIRD fill light was tried and removed after a hard GPU crash (device removed / page fault) showed up in the same session it was added - see the removal note in the .cpp. Kept to just these two.

properties.name: LockedExposure
properties.doc: Locked scene exposure (EV100-ish). Auto-exposure ramps way up in the near-black of space, then blows out the instant a lit planet fills the view - the white wash you saw up close. Pinning min == max exposure removes the adaptation so planets read the same at every range. Higher = brighter overall image.

properties.name: FillLight
properties.doc: Fill lighting + exposure lock (see bEnableFillLighting). Always-on, unlike the SkyAtmosphere sun which only appears over atmosphere-bearing planets.

classes.name: UCosmicFlightComponent
classes.doc: Superman flight + planetary walking gravity for a Character. - DOUBLE-TAP JUMP to toggle between on-foot and flight, either direction. - Flying: cruise along the camera at FlySpeed * Throttle (W/S = throttle, 0 = hover). SHIFT engages the afterburner: boost SPOOLS UP over BurnerSpoolTime until it hits BoostMultiplier, and stays lit until toggled off (spools back down). - On foot the same burner drives sprint: engage and your run speed ramps toward BaseWalk * SprintMultiplier. - ACosmicHUD reads the getters below to draw the tach/speedometer.

functions.name: ApplyWorldOffset
functions.sig: virtual void ApplyWorldOffset(const FVector& InOffset, bool bWorldShift) override;
functions.doc: A world-origin rebase shifts the owning Character (and every ordinary actor) automatically, but CarryPrevXform is just cached FTransform data, not a scene component transform - the engine has no way to know it needs correcting. Left stale for one frame, the very next tick's ride math (which diffs the character's CURRENT, already-corrected position against this OLD, uncorrected cached transform) computes a bogus one-frame delta, i.e. exactly the fine periodic "skating"/jitter reported while riding a planet. Shift it in step.

functions.name: GetShipHullFraction
functions.sig: float GetShipHullFraction() const { return ShipHull / FMath::Max(MaxShipHull, 1.0f); }
functions.doc: Current hull. Restored whenever a fresh ship is called in.

functions.name: IsInvulnerable
functions.doc: True while the post-death invulnerability window is running.

functions.name: ApplyCrashDamage
functions.sig: void ApplyCrashDamage(float Damage, const FVector& ImpactPoint);
functions.doc: Apply a crash/impact to the ship: shields first, then hull. Destroys the ship (and drops the pilot out) when the hull is spent.

functions.name: DestroyShip
functions.doc: Blow up the ship and put the pilot in its place, invulnerable briefly.

functions.name: GetWalkLookFrame
functions.sig: bool GetWalkLookFrame(FVector& OutUp, float& OutYawSign, float& OutPitchSign) const;
functions.doc: Returns the local gravity frame for on-foot mouse look. True only when walking on a body (not flying / in deep space); OutUp is the surface normal at the character, and the signs fold in the invert flags above. ACosmicPlayerCameraManager calls this to steer look in the local frame.

functions.name: GetRideRotationDelta
functions.doc: riding anything, and identity in any frame this component has not ticked in - the value is frame-stamped, so a camera update with no flight tick in front of it can neither re-apply nor miss it. (It was read-and-clear for one revision; that broke the moment a second reader needed it.) WHY THIS EXISTS. The ride moves the character's FRAME, and until 2026-09-01 exactly one consumer of that frame was never told: the view. ACosmicPlayerCameraManager::ProcessViewRotation derives the walk heading by projecting the PREVIOUS frame's world-space forward onto the local horizon - and on a spinning planet that horizon rotates every frame while the forward does not. Standing perfectly still with no mouse input, the heading therefore slid and the elevation drifted, which reads exactly as "the camera rolls around wildly once the planet gets spinning". Building on a planet is what spins it up, which is why it presented as a build bug.

functions.name: SetSpawnPointHere
functions.doc: Record the character's current location as the respawn point.

functions.name: ClearCustomSpawnPoint
functions.doc: Revert to respawning at the PlayerStart.

functions.name: RefreshFlameEffect
functions.doc: Spawn the burner Niagara system if FlameSystem is set and it has not been spawned yet. Idempotent. This exists because FlameSystem is assigned by ACosmicDemoManager, which finds the pawn during Tick - AFTER BeginPlay has already run. While this component was created at runtime by that same manager the ordering was the other way round and BeginPlay could simply read the value. Now that it is a default subobject on ARSSCharacter (see the CosmicFlight declaration there for why), BeginPlay runs first and the assignment would otherwise arrive too late to ever produce a flame.

functions.name: IsOnFootAirborne
functions.doc: On-foot airborne state - jumping or falling while walking. Read this instead of UCharacterMovementComponent::IsFalling(). On foot the CMC is parked in MOVE_None and this component fully owns surface movement, so IsFalling() is ALWAYS false no matter what the character is doing. An Anim Blueprint wired to IsFalling() therefore never leaves the ground states, which is why jump animations never played.

functions.name: IsAirborne
functions.sig: bool IsAirborne() const { return bOnFootAirborne || bFlying; }
functions.doc: Airborne for animation purposes: jumping, falling, or in flight.

functions.name: GetAltitudeFraction
functions.doc: 0 at the surface, 1 at AtmosphereFraction of the body radius and beyond. What a sky anchor fades on: a sky that snaps in at a hard distance reads as a bug, and one that never fades follows you into orbit.

functions.name: ForceRespawn
functions.doc: Teleport home (black hole death, shield breach).

functions.name: NotifyTeleported
functions.doc: Tell the flight controller the pawn was moved by something other than it - a portal, a warp command, any teleport. The reference-frame carry works by differencing the ridden planet's transform frame to frame and applying that delta to the character, which is what lets you stand on a planet that is hurtling through the arena. After a teleport that difference is meaningless: it describes a journey the character did not make, and applying it flings the body across the map. Dropping the carry makes the next frame re-seed from wherever the pawn now actually is. Airborne state is cleared for the same reason - the old ground normal belongs to a surface that may be kilometres away. NewWorldVelocity is the motion the pawn should ARRIVE with, already in world space. A portal passes the entry velocity rotated into the exit's frame; a plain warp passes zero.

functions.name: RequestRecall
functions.doc: Queue a recall to run at the start of the next tick. The HUD calls this (from DrawHUD) so the heavy world-origin rebase inside ForceRespawn never runs mid-render.

functions.name: IsPawnDead
functions.doc: True while the pawn's stats component reports it dead. Movement, the jump and the ability bar all consult this, so "dead" means one thing everywhere rather than each system deciding for itself what a corpse is allowed to do.

functions.name: IsUiCapturingInput
functions.doc: True while a menu owns the mouse and keyboard - options, inventory, map, the death screen, or the CTRL free-cursor toggle. ONE definition, consulted by every gameplay input path. Previously each system decided for itself: melee and abilities checked bShowMouseCursor, while camera look, walking and flight didn't check anything at all - so clicking a slider also swung the camera, and WASD walked the character around behind an open panel. A cursor being visible has to mean the game is not listening, everywhere, or it means nothing.

functions.name: RespawnFromDeath
functions.doc: Clear death, refill the pools and warp home. Driven by the death screen's Respawn button - there is deliberately no timer, so the player can sit dead for as long as they like.

functions.name: ConsumeNetState
functions.doc: Playback side, called by UCosmicPlayerRepComponent::OnRep_NetState. Was this class's own OnRep_NetState body before the wire moved out.

functions.name: AdoptServerReportedState
functions.doc: Server side, called by UCosmicPlayerRepComponent::Server_ReportState_ Implementation after it relays. Was this class's own Server_ReportState_Implementation body (minus the ordering check and the relay, both of which are wire bookkeeping and stayed on the rep component).

functions.name: ConsumeMountVisual
functions.doc: Playback side, called by UCosmicPlayerRepComponent::OnRep_MountVisual.

functions.name: AdoptServerReportedMountVisual
functions.doc: Server side, called by UCosmicPlayerRepComponent:: Server_ReportMountVisual_Implementation after it relays.

functions.name: PublishMountVisual
functions.doc: Owner-side: publish the mount currently configured on this component. Call after writing MountMeshAsset / MountMeshScale / MountMeshRotation / MountMeshOffset. ACosmicDemoManager does exactly that and then calls this. Builds the wire struct from those fields and hands it to UCosmicPlayerRepComponent::PublishMountVisual to get it onto the wire.

functions.name: HasMovementAuthority
functions.doc: Does THIS machine run the full movement simulation for this pawn? True on exactly one machine per pawn: whoever holds its input. That is the owning client for a remote player, the server for its own listen-server pawn or an AI pawn, and the single process in standalone. The unpossessed-on-authority case is not an edge case for tidiness: a pawn spawned by the game mode has no controller until RestartPlayer possesses it, and with the character load now going through an async hub fetch that window is not always one frame. Nobody else can simulate it, so the authority does.

functions.name: CaptureInput
functions.doc: Read every live input device exactly once and freeze the result. The ONLY place below BeginPlay that is allowed to touch APlayerController for input. If a new control is added, it is added here - a poll anywhere downstream is a replay bug that will not show up until reconciliation is running, and will be miserable to find then.

functions.name: ExitFlight
functions.doc: Reason is diagnostic only. There are six separate paths that can drop the pilot out of the ship and they behave very differently - one of them places you on a surface, the others just stop flying wherever you happen to be. Tagging each one is the only way to tell from a screenshot which fired, and at what altitude, without guessing.

functions.name: UpdateBurner
functions.sig: void UpdateBurner(const FCosmicMoveInput& In, float DeltaTime);

functions.name: OnOwnerHit
functions.sig: void OnOwnerHit(AActor* SelfActor, AActor* OtherActor, FVector NormalImpulse, const FHitResult& Hit);

functions.name: HandleCrashImpact
functions.sig: void HandleCrashImpact(class ACelestialBody* Body, const FHitResult& Hit);
functions.doc: Bounce/skid off a planet surface and charge the impact as crash damage.

functions.name: EnsureRideBodyWalkable
functions.doc: EFFECTS. Turns on a body's real mesh collision so the ground probe/facet sweep that runs immediately afterward, THIS SAME FRAME, hits triangles instead of the analytic collision sphere. Idempotent (always sets true) and cheap, so calling it again during a future replay is harmless, just redundant with ACosmicDemoManager's own proximity pass.

functions.name: LogGroundTruthOnce
functions.doc: EFFECTS. The GROUND-TRUTH-ONCE diagnostic (fires only when the body underfoot changes). Reads the ground hit; writes nothing but LastReportedGroundBody, which exists purely to de-duplicate this log.

functions.name: UpdateCameraSmoothedUp
functions.doc: EFFECTS. Damped, camera-only copy of CurrentSurfaceUp - see CameraSmoothedUp in the header. Consumed only by GetWalkLookFrame.

functions.name: ShowFlightFrameDebug
functions.sig: void ShowFlightFrameDebug(const FQuat& ShipQuat, const FVector& Pos) const;
functions.doc: EFFECTS. The in-flight FRAME diagnostic HUD text (bShowFrameDebug).

functions.name: ApplyOnFootCameraAndVisuals
functions.doc: EFFECTS. On-foot camera boom inheritance, the camera manager's view-angle limits, and the run-cycle anim-rate scale - none of these feed gravity, the walk vector or the capsule.

functions.name: CaptureNetState
functions.doc: Snapshot the live movement state into a wire struct.

functions.name: PublishLocalState
functions.doc: Owner side: capture, decide whether it is worth a packet, send it.

functions.name: TickRemoteProxy
functions.doc: Playback side: advance the render clock and place the proxy on it.

functions.name: SampleNetLocation
functions.doc: State at a point on the SERVER's timeline, in this machine's local frame. Interpolates between two received snapshots when the time falls between them; extrapolates off the newest when it does not.

functions.name: NetworkTimeSeconds
functions.doc: The sender's clock, on the server's timeline. See FCosmicPawnState::ServerTime.

functions.name: ApplyFlightVisuals
functions.doc: The COSMETIC half of EnterFlight/ExitFlight - the mount hull, the character mesh's visibility and the burner flame - split out so a proxy, which never runs the movement half, can still show the ship. Before this split the mesh swap lived inline in EnterFlight and consequently happened only on the pilot's own screen: everyone else watched an Aurora fly.

properties.name: MaxJumpHoldSeconds
properties.doc: Longest a jump can be sustained by holding the key (seconds). Together with MaxJumpHeight this fully defines the jump: the climb rate is simply MaxJumpHeight / MaxJumpHoldSeconds, so holding for the full duration lifts you exactly MaxJumpHeight and a tap gives a short hop off the same arc.

properties.name: MaxJumpHeight
properties.doc: Greatest height a single fully-held jump can gain, in cm (2000 = 20 m). The climb stops the moment EITHER this or MaxJumpHoldSeconds is reached, so the ceiling holds even under a weaker/stronger planet's gravity.

properties.name: AirAlignSeconds
properties.doc: that pulls them back down is the planet, along the radial. Those two axes are tens of degrees apart on a die planet, and the arc between them is exactly what makes a jump on a polyhedron feel like a jump rather than a rail. The frame therefore does NOT snap, and just as importantly it does not do most of its turning at the START. An exponential approach (the first attempt here) is fastest in its opening moments, which put the entire rotation into the takeoff - the most jarring possible place to put it, because that is exactly when the player is reading the launch. The curve is now an EASE-IN instead: barely anything for the first half, the bulk of it near the top of the arc where the eye is already following a change of direction. Note this rotates the VIEW only - the trajectory comes from AirVelocity and radial gravity and is not affected by any of this.

properties.name: AirAlignCurvePower
properties.doc: SHAPE of that swing. 1 = linear (constant turn rate). Higher values push more of the rotation toward the end: at 3 the frame has turned only about 12% of the way at the halfway point and the rest arrives late. Below 1 front-loads the turn, which is the jarring behaviour this replaced - kept adjustable rather than hardcoded because how late is "too late" is a feel judgement.

properties.name: GroundedMaxOutwardSpeed
properties.doc: Fastest OUTWARD radial speed that still counts as standing on the ground, cm/s. The gate between "riding up a facet" and "jumping". It was effectively zero (1 cm/s), which is correct on a flat die face and wrong on a sphere: the planet mesh is a 192-segment polyhedron, and running across it at ~600 cm/s lifts you roughly 10 cm/s every time you climb one. Grounded therefore dropped and recovered several times a second - the jitter, and the gnd=1/air=1 flapping, on the sun specifically because it is the only smooth sphere in the system that anyone walks on. A jump leaves at several hundred cm/s, so anything in the low hundreds separates the two cleanly. Too high and a jump gets cancelled by an instant re-snap on its first tick; too low and the flapping returns.

properties.name: SurfaceAlignTurnRate
properties.doc: Degrees/sec cap on how fast the surface-aligned up may turn. Rate-limiting stops a trace that flickers between two facet normals at a seam from teleporting the physics frame every tick (the old "character and camera roll fighting each other" problem near edges).

properties.name: CameraUpSmoothRate
properties.doc: How fast the CAMERA's horizon catches up to the physics frame, per second. Purely cosmetic damping and deliberately slower than the body: running over facets flips the measured ground normal constantly, and every one of those flips used to be handed straight to the view. Letting the camera lag lets the body react at full speed while the horizon ignores the chatter. Raise it toward SurfaceAlignTurnRate for a tighter, twitchier view; lower it for a floatier one. Exposed in Settings > Controls as "Camera Steadying" (1-30). Raised from the first pass's 6.0 - that damped the wobble but made re-levelling after a genuine slope change too sluggish.

properties.name: bSnapCameraUpOnLanding
properties.doc: Adopt the new surface frame OUTRIGHT on a fresh landing instead of easing into it. Requested 2026-09-06: "can we remove that re-orientation time completely and snap the camera upright when they land?" The damping in UpdateCameraSmoothedUp exists for facet-seam CHATTER during continuous contact - running over a die's folds flips the measured normal every few frames and the view used to hunt. A touchdown is not chatter: it is a new frame, known good, and easing into it is exactly the re-orientation lag. Damping still applies while walking.

properties.name: UnjumpedGroundStickySeconds
properties.doc: into space". A jump still works exactly as before. 2.5 s was far too short, and the 09-06 log says why. Airborne episodes START at 38-57 cm/s - the player is not being flung anywhere, they gently lose contact - and then run to **13.9 seconds**. Gravity cannot be what keeps them up; the planet is simply leaving, at up to MaxPoolSpeed (3 km/s, and `rideLin` sits pinned there after a bomb). Once the grace expires the ride is gone and the planet is already kilometres away, so nothing recovers - which is the "thrown off" the player sees. So the number has to outlast the event, not the twitch. 30 s is effectively "until you jump", which is the actual rule being expressed: a departure you CHOSE ends the ride, and nothing else does. A player who walks off an edge still falls - gravity is radial and the ride does not prevent falling, it prevents the planet leaving without you.

properties.name: bShowFrameDebug
properties.doc: Print the on-foot frame (body underfoot, measured up, probe axis, character tilt from world up) to the screen every tick. On by default while the inverted-spawn case is still unexplained - turn it off here once the reading has been captured.

properties.name: bAutoLandOnContact
properties.doc: --- Crash / hull --- Auto-landing on planet contact. OFF: flying into a surface is a CRASH now - the ship bounces and skids instead of politely setting down.

properties.name: CrashLethalSpeed
properties.doc: Closing speed (cm/s) at which a single impact does FULL hull damage. Damage scales with the SQUARE of speed between the safe speed and this, so light taps are trivial and fast impacts are catastrophic (energy, not velocity).

properties.name: CrashBounce
properties.doc: Fraction of speed retained bouncing off a surface (0 = stick, 1 = perfect bounce). Kept low so a crash tumbles and skids rather than pinballing.

properties.name: CrashSkidFriction
properties.doc: Fraction of ALONG-surface speed kept per impact - the skid. 1 = frictionless. This and CrashBounce together ARE the landing model - there is no separate "was this a good landing" test anywhere. Low bounce + high friction (low value here) plants the ship on contact; raise this toward 1 and a shallow approach will skate for kilometres before it sheds enough speed to settle.

properties.name: CrashEnergyScale
properties.doc: Overall severity of impact damage. Damage is computed from the velocity the collision actually destroyed, squared and normalised against CrashLethalSpeed - this scales the whole curve without introducing a cutoff. 0 = indestructible ship, physics unchanged; 2 = twice as fragile.

properties.name: MaxShipHull
properties.doc: Ship hull. Only takes damage once the shields covering that hit are gone.

properties.name: PostDeathInvulnSeconds
properties.doc: Seconds the character is untouchable after their ship is destroyed.

properties.name: JumpDoubleTapSeconds
properties.doc: Double-tap the jump key within this window (seconds) to toggle between on-foot and flight, in either direction, at any time. Replaces the old hold-to-take-off / hold-to-land timers.

properties.name: FlySpeed
properties.doc: Cruise speed at full throttle without burner, cm/s. 55556 cm/s = 2000 kph (1 cm/s = 0.036 kph). The afterburner (SHIFT) multiplies this by BoostMultiplier for traversal; drop BoostMultiplier to 1 for a hard cap.

properties.name: EngineAccel
properties.doc: Engine thrust: how fast the ship builds toward the throttle's target speed (cm/s^2). 18500 spools 0 -> 2000 kph in ~3 s (eases near top). Lower = heavier ship, higher = snappier.

properties.name: EngineBrake
properties.doc: Engine braking: how fast speed bleeds off when you ease the throttle or reverse (cm/s^2).

properties.name: MountMeshAsset
properties.doc: Mesh shown in place of the character while flying with a Mount item equipped. Defaults to the engine cone placeholder - point this at your own ship asset (e.g. /Game/Ships/SM_Scout.SM_Scout) to replace it.

properties.name: MountMeshScale
properties.doc: Local scale applied to MountMeshAsset. The stock cone is scaled up (1.6, 1.0, 3.2) to read as a hull; a real ship mesh will usually want (1, 1, 1) here instead.

properties.name: MountMeshRotation
properties.doc: Local rotation applied to MountMeshAsset (the stock cone points along Z, so it's pitched -90 deg to point along X/forward).

properties.name: MountMeshOffset
properties.doc: Local offset applied to MountMeshAsset, relative to the character root.

properties.name: BoostMultiplier
properties.doc: Fully-spooled afterburner speed multiplier.

properties.name: AtmosphereDrag
properties.doc: Flight speed multiplier while inside a planet's atmosphere (drag). 1 = no effect. 0.5 = you're cut to half speed as you plunge into the air.

properties.name: WaterDrag
properties.doc: Flight speed multiplier while below a water shell surface (heavy drag).

properties.name: BurnerSpoolTime
properties.doc: Seconds of held Shift to spool the burner from 0 to full. HOLD always fills: every press starts charging immediately, with no "already charged, so this press cancels instead" special case - that case used to require a deliberate second press-while-stationary and was easy to trip by accident. Releasing after a genuine hold keeps the level reached (see BurnerQuickTapWindow for what counts as "genuine").

properties.name: BurnerQuickTapWindow
properties.doc: A press-and-release shorter than this (seconds) is a TAP, not a HOLD, and resets the gauge to 0 instead of leaving whatever sliver of charge accumulated during the tap. This is the deliberate "turn the burner back off" gesture; anything held longer just stops climbing and keeps its level, per BurnerSpoolTime above.

properties.name: ThrottleRate
properties.doc: Throttle change per second while holding W / S. 0 = full stop (hover).

properties.name: DefaultThrottle
properties.doc: Throttle the instant you enter flight. 0 = lift off at a dead stop and spool up under your own throttle (no more launching forward at speed).

properties.name: SprintMultiplier
properties.doc: Sprint: fully-spooled burner multiplier on ground speed. At 4x on top of the 1200 cm/s base that's ~170 km/h - a ~5 km planet laps in ~11 min.

properties.name: AlignSpeed
properties.doc: How fast the capsule reorients to gravity / flight direction.

properties.name: bInstantTurnFromStandstill
properties.doc: SNAP TO FACING WHEN SETTING OFF FROM A STANDSTILL. The character normally eases round to its direction of travel at AlignSpeed, which is right while running - a mid-run direction change should arc, not teleport. Standing still it is wrong: the body pirouettes on the spot before it will move, which is the "turn in place" animation that has to be waited out before control feels connected. With this on, the very first frame of movement after a stop faces the new direction instantly and the character just goes. Only that transition is affected; once moving, AlignSpeed is back in charge.

properties.name: MaxStepUpHeight
properties.doc: How high an obstacle the character can walk straight over, in cm. The on-foot controller commits its walk as a single swept move, so before this existed ANY blocking hit stopped you dead - a 10 cm lip of terrain or the corner of a build piece was a wall. 45 cm is knee height on this 180 cm character, which is the height people intuitively expect to step over without thinking about it.

properties.name: MouseYawSens
properties.doc: --- Ship flight controls (6DOF; the camera rides behind the ship) --- Mouse steering sensitivity while flying (degrees per mouse unit). The mouse yaws and pitches the ship; A/D roll it.

properties.name: ShipRollRate
properties.doc: A/D roll rate while flying (degrees per second).

properties.name: bInvertFlightPitch
properties.doc: Default ON: mouse-forward pitches the nose down, matching the on-foot look default (bInvertLookPitch, also ON) and standard flight-stick feel.

properties.name: bInvertLookYaw
properties.doc: --- On-foot look (local-frame camera on a planet surface) --- Flip if walking mouse LEFT/RIGHT (yaw) turns the wrong way. Toggle in the editor - no rebuild needed.

properties.name: bInvertLookPitch
properties.doc: Flip if walking mouse UP/DOWN (pitch) is inverted. Toggle in the editor. Default ON (mouse-up looks down) to match the preferred on-foot feel.

properties.name: GravitySwitchHysteresis
properties.doc: A new gravity body must pull this much harder to steal the character.

properties.name: GlobalGravityScale
properties.doc: Global multiplier on on-foot surface gravity. Live-tunable from the options menu (1 = as authored on each planet).

properties.name: WalkSpeedScale
properties.doc: Global multiplier on on-foot walk speed. Live-tunable from the options menu.

properties.name: FlameSystem
properties.doc: Burning trail while flying (optional; the fallback light always works).

properties.name: ExplosionSystem
properties.doc: Burst played where the ship dies. Optional - the ship still explodes mechanically without it, just silently.

properties.name: RespawnLocation
properties.doc: Where to respawn after being devoured by a black hole.

properties.name: bHasCustomSpawn
properties.doc: A player-set spawn point, stored as an OFFSET from the PlayerStart so it survives world-origin rebasing (both points shift together, so their difference is invariant). Respawn prefers this over the PlayerStart.

properties.name: SetSpawnKey
properties.doc: Optional direct key for setting the spawn point. UNBOUND by default. This used to be H, alongside a "Set Home" button on the primary bar. Both are gone: Set Home is a spellbook entry now, so it can be dragged onto any hotkey the player actually wants it on, and holding H hostage for a once-every-few-minutes action was poor value for a letter key. Bind a key here if you want the old behaviour back - the poll below still honours it.

properties.name: bAllowWorldOriginRebase
properties.doc: Shift the world origin onto the character after a long-range teleport. Default OFF. It protects float precision at astronomical coordinates, but this arena is ~47 km across and never needs it - while the rebase itself teleports every actor in the level in a single frame, which flung the planet field apart and tripped the renderer's stale-light-cache ensure on every recall. Turn it on only for genuinely system-scale travel.

properties.name: MinRebaseShiftCm
properties.doc: Minimum teleport distance (cm) that justifies a rebase, when enabled. Deliberately larger than the whole arena.

properties.name: StableGroundCoyoteSeconds
properties.doc: Grace period during which a StableGround floor (the station, a build piece) keeps the ride frame and the up-vector even though we are airborne. Long enough for a hop or a missed probe, far too short to survive an actual jump toward a planet - which must still re-capture, or the "cannot land on a planet I have never landed on" deadlock comes straight back.

properties.name: ShipMesh
properties.doc: Placeholder starship shown while flying with a Mount item equipped (the character mesh is hidden). Swap the mesh asset later for a real ship.

classes.name: ACosmicGroundEnemy
classes.doc: A creature that walks a planet's surface and fights the player on foot. It uses the SAME radial-gravity idea the player controller does - stick to the body underfoot, orient up away from its centre - but in a deliberately cheap form. There is no pathfinding: navmesh doesn't exist on a tumbling polyhedron that teleports itself every frame, so this walks the tangent plane directly toward its target and lets the ground probe keep it on the hull. Health lives in UCosmicStatsComponent, exactly like the player's, so a single damage path serves both and nothing needs to special-case "is this an enem…

functions.name: SurfaceUp
functions.doc: Outward radial at our position - "up" for this creature.

functions.name: StickToSurface
functions.doc: Keep the feet on the hull and the body oriented to it.

functions.name: UpdateLocomotion
functions.doc: Drive the mesh's locomotion clip from our own measured speed.

functions.name: ApplyKnockback
functions.doc: Shove this creature. Called by whatever lands a hit, so knockback comes from the striker's direction and strength rather than being invented here.

properties.name: Body
properties.doc: SciFiTrooper skeletal body, with its own anim blueprint driving idle/walk.

properties.name: SightRange
properties.doc: Notices the player within this range (cm).

properties.name: LeashRange
properties.doc: Gives up and returns to post beyond this (cm). Larger than SightRange so it doesn't flicker between chase and idle at the boundary.

properties.name: StrikeWindup
properties.doc: Windup before a strike connects. Gives the player a window to back out of range, which is what makes the fight readable rather than a damage aura.

properties.name: GravityAccel
properties.doc: How hard it sticks to the surface (cm/s^2). Keeps it on the hull without running the full player controller.

properties.name: HomeBody
properties.doc: Body this creature lives on. Auto-detected at BeginPlay from whatever is nearest, then it rides that body's motion.

classes.name: FCosmicHotbarSlot
classes.doc: One slot on the ability hotbar. The definition comes from the CockpitAbility

properties.name: Ability
properties.doc: Ability data (name, icon, category, cooldown, ...) from the cockpit model.

properties.name: Key
properties.doc: Key that activates this slot.

properties.name: GamepadKey
properties.doc: Gamepad button for the same slot. Separate from Key so a controller player can see and rebind their own layout instead of inheriting keyboard keys - the flight hotbar (laser, torpedo, boost, ascend) previously had no gamepad bindings anywhere in the options menu.

properties.name: LandName
properties.doc: ON-FOOT name for this slot, when it differs from the flight name. The first four slots are flight actions - Laser, Torpedo, Boost, Ascend - and showing those words while walking around is simply wrong: on land the same four inputs are your right hand, left hand, sprint and jump. One slot carrying both labels keeps a single binding per input (rebind once, correct in both contexts) instead of two parallel bars that could disagree. Empty = the flight name is used everywhere.

properties.name: bRecall
properties.doc: If set, the HUD invokes "warp to your set spawn" when pressed.

classes.name: ACosmicHUD
classes.doc: Canvas HUD: a modern screen-space rework of the cockpit UI. - bottom-centre ability/spell hotbar (data-driven from FCockpitAbilityDefinition) with impactful spring-physics press feedback and cooldown sweeps, - corner tach/speedometer, crosshair, shield quadrants, - a settings menu (graphics / audio / control rebinding) reachable by the on-screen cog button (PIE-safe), a hotkey, or Escape. Installed at runtime by ACosmicDemoManager via ClientSetHUD.

functions.name: PushDamagePopup
functions.sig: void PushDamagePopup(const FVector& WorldPos, float Amount, bool bIncoming);
functions.doc: Float a damage number in the world. Called from anything that deals or takes damage, so it has to be public. bIncoming = damage TO the player, drawn red and larger so being hit is impossible to miss.

functions.name: IsPointerOverHud
functions.doc: True when the pointer is over anything the UI owns - a bar slot, the mini-map, the cog, the spell button, or anywhere inside an open panel. Build mode asks this before placing: mouse-placement legitimately runs with the cursor up, so "is a cursor visible" can no longer be the test for whether a click belongs to the world or to the interface. Uses the rects each element recorded as it drew, so it is always in step with what is actually on screen this frame.

functions.name: UiOwnsScrollWheel
functions.doc: True when a mouse wheel notch this frame belongs to the interface rather than to the camera. Camera zoom lives in the character Blueprint, which has no idea a menu is open - so scrolling a long settings tab also dollied the camera in and out behind it. Rather than require the Blueprint to be edited, the flight component asks this and simply holds the spring arm still while it is true. Covers open windows (only while the pointer is actually inside one, so the wheel still zooms when a window is off to the side), the system map, and build mode - all three already spend the wheel on something.

functions.name: AddLog
functions.sig: void AddLog(const FString& Text, const FLinearColor& Color = FLinearColor::White);
functions.doc: Append a line to the event log / chat pane. Public because gameplay code outside the HUD needs to tell the player things - an ability that has no montage and no damage number (Set Home, Recall) has no other way to confirm the press registered. Long lines are word-wrapped to the pane.

functions.name: UI
functions.doc: Global multiplier for every UI dimension. Derived from the viewport height against a 1080p baseline, then multiplied by the player's own preference, so text stays the same APPARENT size at any resolution.

functions.name: WinUI
functions.doc: Same resolution baseline as UI(), but multiplied by WindowScalePref rather than UIScalePref. HUD Scale used to drive BOTH the always-on HUD (vitals, hotbars, minimap) and the pop-up windows (settings, spellbook, inventory), so sizing the hotbar to taste silently resized every menu with it. Those are two unrelated judgements - how big the overlay should be while playing, versus how big a dialog should be while reading it - so they get two sliders. Every windowed panel measures itself with this; everything else uses UI().

functions.name: CloseTopWindow
functions.doc: Close the most recently opened window. Returns false if none were open.

functions.name: DismissWindow
functions.doc: Close one window properly: stack entry AND the per-panel bool that is the real source of truth. Shared by Esc and the title-bar X so the two can never drift apart.

functions.name: EndWindow
functions.doc: Record how tall the content turned out and draw the scrollbar.

functions.name: InClip
functions.sig: bool InClip(float X, float Y, float W, float H) const;
functions.doc: True if the rect is at least partly inside the active clip (or none is set).

functions.name: LoadSurfaces
functions.doc: UI surface textures pulled from /Game/AutomotiveMaterials. Canvas can only reliably draw TEXTURES (a surface-domain material has no meaning without a light), so the panels use the carbon-fibre base colour map directly - which is the same surface those materials present anyway.

functions.name: DrawGauge

functions.name: TickSlotFx

functions.doc: --- Inventory / equipment panel (I / left stick click) ---

functions.name: DrawMap
functions.doc: --- System map (M / right stick click) --- Orthographic top-down plot of the arena, drawn straight from the celestial subsystem's body list. No render target and no second camera: the bodies already know where they are and how big they are, so a projection onto the canvas is both cheaper and always current.

functions.name: InitHotbar
functions.doc: --- Flight / utility slots (now drawn as part of the combined primary bar) --- Seeds Hotbar with Laser, Torpedo, Set Home, Recall. Sprint/Jump are deliberately NOT here any more - see the PrimaryBar block above.

functions.name: DrawPortalLabels
functions.doc: --- Appearance mannequins (walk up, press to change body) ---------------- Proximity and the key both live here rather than on the mannequin actor. "Which one is nearest" is a single per-frame decision, and having each mannequin answer it for itself means N actors racing to claim a prompt in whatever order they happen to tick. Every other binding in the game is a HUD member too, so the settings menu already knows how to rebind this. Owner name floating over every portal in view. Drawn on the canvas rather than as a world-space text component: the tag has to stay upright and legible at any distance and from any angle, which a 3D text render would fight, and the HUD already projects world points for damage popups and the target indicator.

functions.name: DrawPortalShop
functions.doc: --- Portal wardrobe / shop ------------------------------------------------ Opens from a key ANYWHERE for re-equipping, but the Buy buttons only light up while you are stood at a vendor. That split is the whole design: owning and wearing are free, acquiring costs you a trip.

functions.name: DrawHoloSim
functions.doc: --- Holo-sim door --------------------------------------------------------- UNLIKE THE PORTAL SHOP, THIS ONLY OPENS AT THE DOOR. The shop is a wardrobe you carry; this is a physical airlock into another world, and there is no coherent way to step through one from the middle of the deck. The list itself lives on AHoloSimDoor, not here. Fetching it is a network round trip and travelling to an instance is a multi-second state machine - neither survives on a HUD that is rebuilt every frame. Takes no controller: everything it needs is on the door actor.

functions.name: TickRmbLook
functions.doc: Poll RMB and drive the camera while held. Returns true while capturing.

functions.name: TickChatInput
functions.sig: void TickChatInput(class APlayerController* PC, float Dt);
functions.doc: Poll printable keys / Backspace / Enter / Escape into ChatInput.

functions.name: DrawChatInput
functions.doc: Draw the input box under the log when chat is open.

functions.name: SubmitChatLine
functions.sig: void SubmitChatLine(const FString& Line, class APlayerController* PC);

functions.name: TickTargeting
functions.doc: Poll the targeting keys and validate the current target.

functions.sig: void CycleTarget(class APlayerController* PC, int32 Dir);
functions.doc: Step through the cycle list. Dir +1 forward, -1 backward (Shift+Tab).

functions.name: DrawTargetPanel
functions.doc: Name + health panel, top-centre.

functions.doc: Ring drawn around the target in the world.

functions.name: IsTargetValid
functions.doc: True if the actor is alive and still a legal selection.

functions.name: DrawMiniMap
functions.doc: --- Mini-map (upper-right, below the cog) --- Rotates with the player's heading so "up" is always where you face.

functions.name: ApplyCursor
functions.sig: void ApplyCursor(class APlayerController* PC, bool bWantCursor, bool bForce);
functions.doc: Single authority for cursor visibility + input mode. Called only from HandleToggle so bShowMouseCursor and the input mode can never desync (the old cog/close/death writers each set the flag WITHOUT the input mode, which is what stranded the mouse "behind" the game after CTRL / inventory).

functions.name: DrawButton

functions.doc: Seed Elem[] with this HUD's DEFAULT layout (vitals upper-left, spell bars lower-right, gauge top-middle at 80%, log lower-left, minimap upper-right). Called once on the first draw and again by Edit UI's Reset Layout, so "reset" restores these positions rather than a bare screen-corner default.

functions.name: ElemOff
functions.doc: Offset for an element, already multiplied by the global UI scale.

functions.name: ElemScale
functions.doc: Size multiplier for an element.
